archetypes.name: bash-python-parity
archetypes.rationale: This plan mandates identical behavioral changes in two separate implementations (Bash ship-pr.sh and Python ci_monitor.py); plan-level drift between them is the top failure risk.
archetypes.prompt_body: For every behavioral change described in the Bash path (`run_evaluate_failure`, blind-rerun gate, in-progress deferral, exhaustion flag), verify there is an explicitly described equivalent in the Python path (`evaluate_failure`, `ci_monitor.py` fix loop, `monitor` outcome mapping), and vice versa. Check that the `code_fix_attempted_on_ready_log` / `_code_fix_attempted_on_ready_log` predicate, the `jobs_state == "in_progress"` / `ci_failed_rc == 3` deferral branch, and the `fix-exhausted` vs `waterfall-failed` outcome mapping are described with equivalent semantics in both implementations — not just parallel naming. Flag any asymmetry where one implementation block in the plan lacks a corresponding element in the other, or where described decisions diverge beyond surface syntax differences (rc codes vs enum states). Verify that the new Python test cases in `python/test_ci_monitor.py` cover the same behavioral branches as the new Bash helpers in `scripts/test-ship-pr-fix-loop-3334.inc.sh` and the rewritten `ci_fix_exhausted` test. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: exhaustion-predicate
archetypes.rationale: The substantive-attempt predicate is the plan's most complex new invariant; incomplete or internally inconsistent predicate description is a latent plan defect.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan introduces a 'substantive code-fix attempt predicate' that gates whether terminal exhaustion routes to exit 3 (`ci-fix-exhausted`) versus exit 4 (stall). Verify that the predicate's positive and negative conditions are completely and consistently stated across every section of the plan that references it: the Bash file-modification block, the Python file-modification block, the edge-cases section, and the failure-modes section. Check whether every code path described as reaching the exhaustion check has a clearly stated predicate outcome — identify any path (e.g., `vendor_rc == 4`, verification-retry consumption, `run_per_job_local_fix_loop` with `ci_failed_count == 0`) whose predicate outcome is ambiguous or unstated. Verify that the listed test cases collectively exercise all four predicate branches: (1) ready logs + ready jobs + substantive fix ran, (2) ready logs + ready jobs + launcher/push/no-tier only, (3) in-progress-only exhaustion, and (4) logs-not-ready exhaustion. Flag any predicate branch for which no test case is described. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: exit-routing
archetypes.rationale: The new ci-fix-exhausted bail reason must be registered in multiple contract surfaces; a missing registration in any one of them would silently misroute the orchestrator.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan introduces `ci-fix-exhausted` as a new exit-3 bail reason. Verify that the plan explicitly describes updates to every contract surface that must recognize this new bail reason: `needs_user_bail_reason` (~line 1720), `is_autonomous_exit3_bail_reason` (~line 1728), the SKILL.md Step 8+ Exit 3 trigger list (~line 1169), `ci-decide.md` disambiguation prose, and `scripts/ship-pr.md` documentation. Check that each carve-out the plan defines as staying on exit 4 (vendor_loop launcher-only exhaustion, rebase-storm, in-progress-only exhaustion) is explicitly represented in both the file-change section and the test plan — not just mentioned in the edge-cases prose. Verify there is no ambiguity about whether the SKILL.md wording change alone is sufficient to wire `ci-fix-exhausted` into the orchestrator's autonomous CI-fix sub-procedure, or whether additional orchestrator-side parsing of `BAIL_REASON` is required. Check the `scripts/test-implement-step8-exit3-first-fixer.sh` update description covers assertion of both `first-fixer-non-health` and `ci-fix-exhausted` triggering the same sub-procedure. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
